about: Every place the mod touches the game. Each row is one read or write. read_verified / write_verified become true only when the probe or a test in the real game shows it. Field names first came from a third-party script (rkaganda/SF6_replay_capture).

rows.purpose: Detect a new round so per-round state resets (not reliable alone: see evidence)
rows.evidence: Probe 2026-10-07: read 0. In-game panel showed 'round 0' in both round 1 and a later round, so it does not reliably change between rounds; the mod also resets when stage_timer jumps back by more than 30.

rows.purpose: Detect that the match simulation advanced one tick (render frames and sim ticks differ)
Read health to find damage taken and Rage threshold; write it to add bonus damage and chip damage
rows.source: SF6_replay_capture: cPlayer[i].vital_new (read only there; writing is unproven)
rows.evidence: Probe 2026-10-07: both players read 10000 then 9250/10000. Write test: wrote 8349 over 8350; value was still 8349 one frame later (not reverted). Later reads were lower (7749 at 30 frames, 6849 at 120) because P1 was taking damage, not a revert. A bonus write during a real hit is still to be seen.

rows.purpose: Detect the moment a fighter starts blocking (blockstun begins) for Heat chip damage
rows.evidence: Probe 2026-10-07: both players read 0 (not blocking). Value while blocking not seen yet.

rows.purpose: Research only: what SF6 tracks during air combos, to see whether juggle scaling can be changed
rows.evidence: Probe 2026-10-07: both players read -1 (no combo running). Meaning during a combo not seen yet.

rows.purpose: Read the keyboard keys that trigger Heat (REFramework gives raw keys only, no gamepad)
Real maximum health, for the Rage threshold and Heat chip size (replaces remembering the highest health seen)
rows.source: Probe 2026-10-07 field list: vital_max exists on the fighter object

rows.purpose: Tell when a fighter is in hitstun, so the opponent's Heat timer pauses while they are being hit (Tekken 8: the Heat timer stops while the opponent is hit)
rows.source: Fighter field list from the probe; SF6_replay_capture reads it as hitstun
rows.evidence: Field name seen in the probe's field list; its value during hitstun has not been seen yet.

rows.purpose: The game's own held-button bits for each fighter, so Heat can later be started from a gamepad button combo (Tekken's Heat Burst is 2+3) instead of only a keyboard key
rows.source: Fighter field list from the probe; the meaning of the bits is not known yet
rows.evidence: Field name seen in the probe's field list. Which bit is which button is unknown: the panel shows the live value so the bits can be decoded.

rows.purpose: Slow the whole game briefly for dramatic moments (Heat Smash or Rage Art landing)
rows.source: A common REFramework pattern for RE Engine games; not seen working in SF6 yet
rows.evidence: User test 2026-10-07: pressing the panel's test button did not visibly slow the game (whether the call errored is unknown). Either SF6 ignores global speed or the call was refused.

rows.purpose: Research: a candidate for the game's hit freeze, to make hits feel weightier
rows.source: Fighter field list from the probe; meaning unknown
rows.evidence: Field name seen in the probe's field list; value during a hit not seen yet.

rows.purpose: Research: another candidate for the game's hit freeze
rows.source: Fighter field list from the probe; meaning unknown
rows.evidence: Field name seen in the probe's field list; value during a hit not seen yet.

rows.purpose: Research: the hit freeze field the community replay script reads; it was NOT in the fighter field list, so it may not exist on this object
rows.evidence: Not in the probe's field list for the fighter object. The probe will say whether reading it works.

rows.purpose: Second way to slow the game: the current scene's time scale
rows.source: A common REFramework pattern for RE Engine games; not seen working in SF6 yet

rows.purpose: Third way to slow the game: lower the frame cap, which slows anything that advances one step per frame; the original cap is restored afterwards
rows.source: A common REFramework pattern for RE Engine games; not seen working in SF6 yet
